title: Church history: myths and real failures
tagline: The Crusades, Inquisition, Galileo, the “Dark Ages”, witch trials, Pius XII and slavery: what happened, and where the Church was wrong.
whyItMatters: History is often used as a weapon against the faith. Fair-minded answers need both facts and honesty about real sins.

mindset.tip: Do not defend the indefensible. Where the Church failed, say so plainly; John Paul II asked forgiveness for past wrongs.
Ask which event the person means and where they learned it; then check the sources together.
Use historians of different views, including non-Catholic ones. (Proverbs 18:17)
Avoid mocking those who hold the myths; most picked them up from school or film. (1 Peter 3:15-16)

resources.title: Address to the Pontifical Academy of Sciences (31 October 1992)
resources.creator: Pope John Paul II
resources.why: The pope’s own words closing the Church’s review of the Galileo case.

resources.title: Upon Further Review
resources.creator: Christian History magazine
resources.why: A Protestant history magazine retells the Galileo case and the 1992 statement.
resources.note: Protestant source; helpful as a fair outside view.

resources.title: What the Crusades Were Really Like (interview)
resources.creator: Thomas Madden (ZENIT, on EWTN)
resources.why: A historian lays out why the Crusades began and how popular myths took hold.
resources.note: Madden is a Catholic medievalist; some peers dispute parts of his emphasis.

resources.title: What is the Inquisition?
resources.creator: Catholic Answers
resources.why: A short overview of what the Inquisitions were and how they worked.

resources.title: The Myth of the Spanish Inquisition
resources.creator: Catholic Answers
resources.why: Looks at the popular picture and what the records show.
resources.note: Catholic Answers. Estimates of the dead vary between sources, so compare more than one.

resources.title: Did the Church Ever Support Slavery?
resources.creator: Catholic Answers
resources.why: Looks at papal statements and at Catholics who defended or profited from slavery.

resources.title: Crusaders and Historians
resources.creator: Thomas F. Madden (Catholic Culture)
resources.why: A review essay on what recent crusade scholars have overturned.
resources.note: Madden is a Catholic medievalist; some peers dispute parts of his emphasis.

resources.title: The Church’s Most Recent Attempt to Dispel the Galileo Myth
resources.creator: George V. Coyne, S.J.
resources.why: The Vatican Observatory’s director reflects on John Paul II’s 1992 address and the case.
resources.note: By a Jesuit astronomer; candid about the Church’s errors.

resources.title: How Many People Did the Catholic Church Kill?
resources.creator: Catholic Answers
resources.why: Weighs the numbers and the comparisons often used against the Church.
resources.note: Catholic Answers; read the numbers with care.

resources.title: Who Burned the Witches? (Part 1)
resources.creator: Catholic World Report
resources.why: Sets the witch hunts in their time and place, across Catholic and Protestant lands.
resources.note: Catholic outlet; check the figures against a scholar such as Brian Levack.

resources.title: “The Dark Ages”, the Middle Ages and Periodisation
resources.creator: Tim O’Neill (History for Atheists)
resources.why: Separates the real early medieval collapse from the later slur on the whole Middle Ages.
resources.note: By an atheist historian; fair to the Church but not an apologist.

resources.title: Let My People Go: the Catholic Church and Slavery
resources.creator: Mark Brumley (Catholic Culture)
resources.why: Traces Church teaching on slavery from St. Paul to the modern popes.
resources.note: Apologetic in aim; it should be read with the Church’s real failures in mind.

resources.title: The Crusades: A History
resources.creator: Jonathan Riley-Smith
resources.why: A standard scholarly history of the Crusades by a leading historian of the field.
resources.note: Book for purchase (Yale University Press); also in libraries.

resources.title: Did the Pope Apologise to Galileo?
resources.creator: Tim O’Neill (History for Atheists)
resources.why: A sceptical historian checks what the 1992 statement did and did not say.
resources.note: By an atheist historian who often corrects myths on both sides; read critically.

resources.title: Pius XII and the Holocaust
resources.creator: Jonathan Gorsky (Yad Vashem)
resources.why: A Jewish-institution scholar sets out the debate over Pius XII’s silence and rescue work.
resources.note: Published by Yad Vashem; the other side’s own scholarly voice.
